subject: Emergency maintenance: short-notice dependency swap to mitigate inference instability
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: support@nebulaanalytics.com
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Apr 2029 09:15:00 +0000
Subject: Emergency maintenance: short-notice dependency swap to mitigate inference instability

Hi Amir / Nebula team,

We're reaching out with an urgent, short-notice maintenance advisory. Over the last 45 minutes we've detected intermittent tokenization mismatches and occasional truncated streaming responses originating from a third-party attention library (libfastattn) used in our custom kernel path. The issue surfaces at high-concurrency tail workloads and causes a small percentage of in-flight requests to return a token offset error.

What we're doing now (immediate mitigation):
- Initiated an automated dependency swap: affected nodes will fall back to our verified internal kernel (kernel-v2-safe) while we validate a micro-patch to libfastattn. This swap is rolling and targeted — we expect it to reduce errors within ~20–30 minutes for affected capacity.
- Applied a hotfix to the coordinator to force KV-cache alignment when falling back.

Customer impact / actions:
- You may see transient stream disconnects or a small number of partial outputs during the swap window.
- No model data has been exposed; this is a runtime compatibility issue.
- Recommended action: if you see a stuck streaming connection, restart the client session. We have a short remediation checklist attached (remediation_steps.txt) and generated a one-page summary (hotfix_patch_summary.pdf).

ETA: We expect the roll to complete for US regions in approx 35 minutes. We'll post a follow-up when the swap is complete and include smoke-test results.

If you'd prefer us to pause and schedule a maintenance window, let me know immediately; otherwise we'll proceed to reduce the error rate as quickly as possible. Apologies for the disruption — we're treating this as P1 and prioritizing stability.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachments: hotfix_patch_summary.pdf (summary), remediation_steps.txt (short checklist)

From: Amir Patel <amir.patel@nebulaanalytics.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Apr 2029 09:32:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Emergency maintenance: short-notice dependency swap to mitigate inference instability

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the heads up. We saw a couple of truncated responses in our prod stream a little while ago and traced them to the same call traces you described.

Please proceed with the swap; we don't have a maintenance window today and prefer you to prioritize stability. Can you confirm: will existing in-flight requests be retried automatically or will we need to restart any client-side sessions? Also, any expected change to latency while on kernel-v2-safe?

– Amir
Lead ML Engineer, Nebula Analytics
amir.patel@nebulaanalytics.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 30 Apr 2029 11:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Emergency maintenance: short-notice dependency swap to mitigate inference instability

Internal notes / runbook update:
- Swap to kernel-v2-safe completed for us-west-2 and us-east-1 at 11:00 Z (rolling nodes + autoscaler instances). Error rate on affected paths down from ~0.8% -> 0.02% in pilot pool.
- KV-cache alignment guard is active; we applied a coordinator hotfix and validated prefix integrity against a reddis-backed sample set.
- Latency impact: median latency unchanged; P95 increased ~8–12ms on fallback in heavy batches (expected).

Action items:
- Jonas: please coordinate a quick smoke test with Nebula (see contact below) and attach results.
- Grace: open a postmortem doc and capture the dependency call graph and rollback criteria. Link the draft to the incident doc.
- Ben: schedule a sync with Platform Security to confirm no data integrity concerns and to capture evidence for audit.

Quoted for context to external: "On Tue, 30 Apr 2029 09:15:00 +0000 Marissa Cole wrote:"

Attachments: smoke_test_results.log

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Amir Patel <amir.patel@nebulaanalytics.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Apr 2029 13:40:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Emergency maintenance: short-notice dependency swap to mitigate inference instability

Hi Amir — quick follow-up.

Status: the fallback swap completed across your routed capacity at 13:25 Z. Our smoke tests (attached) show no remaining token offset errors and error-rate returned to baseline. In-flight requests that were affected are not automatically retried server-side — we recommend restarting any long-lived streaming client sessions to clear socket state. Our internal autoscaling replaced a small number of nodes during the swap which will have reset outstanding streams.

Observed impact: transient P95 latency bump (~10ms) while kernel-v2-safe is used; otherwise behavior is back to normal.

Next steps:
- We'll publish a short postmortem and remediation plan to the linked drive doc within 48 hours: https://drive.google.com/redwood-postmortem/nebula-dep-swap
- We'll include timeline, root cause (libfastattn regression under concurrent KV patterns), and permanent mitigations (patch to libfastattn + improved integration testing).

If you see anything odd over the next 24h please reply and we'll escalate immediately. Thanks for the quick confirmation to proceed earlier.

Best,
Marissa
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachments: smoke_test_results.log
